title: WASM + Go bindings support
description: Implement WebAssembly and Go FFI bindings for Muxide (GitHub issue #1). Branch: feature/wasm-support. Core Rust FFI layer (src/ffi.rs) and WASM bindings (src/wasm.rs) are scaffolded but need finishing. C header, Go package, CI, and PR still needed.
acceptance_criteria: cargo check --target wasm32-unknown-unknown --features wasm passes. Go example compiles and links. CI green. PR merged.
notes: Branch feature/wasm-support created. Core scaffolding complete: src/wasm.rs (wasm-bindgen API), src/ffi.rs (C FFI layer), Cargo.toml wasm feature flag, into_writer() added to Muxer. Remaining: gate bin target, Go bindings package, CI job, PR.

title: Fix wasm.rs finish() to return output bytes via into_writer()
description: wasm.rs finish() currently returns empty Vec. Must call finish_in_place_with_stats() then into_writer() to retrieve the Vec<u8> output. The into_writer() method was added to Muxer and Mp4Writer but the wasm finish path doesn't use it yet.
acceptance_criteria: WasmMuxer::finish() returns non-empty Vec<u8> containing valid MP4 data
close_reason: wasm.rs finish() already uses into_writer() correctly - verified in code review

title: Gate [[bin]] target so wasm32 builds skip the CLI binary
description: The CLI binary (src/bin/muxide.rs) depends on clap and indicatif which do not compile for wasm32-unknown-unknown. The [[bin]] section in Cargo.toml must be conditional so that cargo check --target wasm32-unknown-unknown --features wasm succeeds without attempting to build the binary.
design: Approach: Add required-features to the [[bin]] section listing a non-wasm feature, OR use [target.'cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))'] autbins. Simplest: add a 'cli' feature that is default-on, gate [[bin]] with required-features = ["cli"], and make cli default. Alternative: just remove [[bin]] and rely on autbins with a cfg gate in the file. Evaluate both, pick the one with least friction.
acceptance_criteria: 1. cargo check --target wasm32-unknown-unknown --no-default-features --features wasm exits 0. 2. cargo build (native) still produces the muxide binary. 3. No conditional compilation attributes needed in src/bin/muxide.rs itself.
close_reason: Gated [[bin]] on cli feature; clap/indicatif made optional + cli-gated so wasm32 builds skip the CLI. Verified native binary builds and wasm32 check passes clean.

title: Create bindings/muxide.h C header matching src/ffi.rs exports
description: Go cgo requires a C header to know function signatures. Write bindings/muxide.h with: opaque typedefs for MuxideMuxer and MuxideFragmentedMuxer, all extern C function declarations from src/ffi.rs, error code constants (MUXIDE_OK=0, MUXIDE_ERR_NULL=-1, etc.), and a MuxideMetadata struct. Every function in ffi.rs must have a matching declaration.
design: Use standard C types: int32_t for error codes, uint8_t for bytes, size_t for lengths. Opaque structs via forward declaration (typedef struct MuxideMuxer MuxideMuxer). No implementation in the header.
acceptance_criteria: 1. gcc -c bindings/muxide.h produces no errors. 2. Every pub extern C fn in src/ffi.rs has a matching declaration in the header. 3. Error constants match the Rust values exactly. 4. Header includes stdint.h and stddef.h for portable types.
notes: Files: bindings/muxide.h (new). Cross-reference: src/ffi.rs function list.
close_reason: Added bindings/muxide.h with opaque handles, all 18 extern C declarations from src/ffi.rs, error constants (MUXIDE_OK=0..MUXIDE_ERR_ALREADY_FINISHED=-4) matching Rust values, and MuxideMetadata struct. Verified with gcc -c (clean) and struct/const parity.

title: Create bindings/go/ package with idiomatic Go wrapper
description: Create a Go package that wraps the C FFI via cgo. Package structure: bindings/go/muxide.go (wrapper), bindings/go/muxide_test.go (unit test), bindings/go/example/main.go (usage demo). The Go API should be idiomatic: NewMuxer(codec, w, h, fps) (*Muxer, error), WriteVideo(pts, data, keyframe) error, WriteAudio(pts, data) error, Finish() ([]byte, error). Use runtime.SetFinalizer for automatic cleanup.
design: cgo directives: #cgo CFLAGS: -I../../bindings, #cgo LDFLAGS: -L../../target/release -lmuxide. Build the .so/.dylib/.dll with cargo rustc --crate-type cdylib. The Go package should NOT expose raw C types. Use []byte for data, float64 for timestamps.
acceptance_criteria: 1. go build ./bindings/go/... exits 0. 2. go vet ./bindings/go/... exits 0. 3. Example in example/main.go compiles. 4. Muxer struct has a Close() method and a finalizer. 5. Error messages from Rust are propagated through muxide_last_error into Go error values.
notes: Files: bindings/go/muxide.go, bindings/go/muxide_test.go, bindings/go/example/main.go (all new). Depends on: muxide-3t8.3 (header must exist first).

title: Add wasm-check job to .github/workflows/ci.yml
description: Add a CI job that verifies the wasm32 build target works. Job name: wasm-check. Runs on ubuntu-latest with stable Rust. Steps: rustup target add wasm32-unknown-unknown, then cargo check --target wasm32-unknown-unknown --features wasm. Should run on push and PR like other jobs.
acceptance_criteria: 1. CI workflow has a wasm-check job. 2. Job passes on the feature/wasm-support branch. 3. Job does NOT run the CLI binary check (that would fail on wasm32). 4. Job runs on both push and pull_request triggers.
close_reason: Added wasm-check job to ci.yml: installs wasm32 target, runs cargo check --target wasm32-unknown-unknown --no-default-features --features wasm (the literal --features wasm fails since cli is default-on). Runs on push/PR via inherited triggers.

title: Final verification, commit, push, and open PR for WASM branch
description: Run the full verification suite: cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings, cargo test, cargo check --target wasm32-unknown-unknown --features wasm. Fix any failures. Commit all changes. Push feature/wasm-support. Open PR against main referencing GitHub issue #1. PR description must explain: what WASM bindings provide, what Go bindings provide, how to build each, architecture diagram in text.
acceptance_criteria: 1. All 4 verification commands exit 0. 2. PR is open on GitHub. 3. PR body references issue #1 (Closes #1 or Refs #1). 4. PR body contains: build instructions for wasm (wasm-pack or cargo + wasm-bindgen-cli), build instructions for Go (cargo rustc --crate-type cdylib + go build), architecture summary. 5. CI on the PR is green.
notes: Depends on: muxide-3t8.2, muxide-3t8.3, muxide-3t8.4, muxide-3t8.5 all closed first.

title: CI/infra hardening
description: Fix CI warnings, address dependabot vulnerability, and harden the release pipeline.
acceptance_criteria: No CI warnings, no dependabot alerts, release workflow tested

title: Fix Node.js 20 deprecation warnings in GitHub Actions
description: CI annotations show: 'Node.js 20 is deprecated. actions/checkout@v4 and actions/cache@v4 target Node.js 20.' Upgrade actions/checkout@v4 to actions/checkout@v5 (if available) or pin to a version that supports Node 24. Same for actions/cache@v4. Also update softprops/action-gh-release@v1 to v2 in release.yml. Check each action's latest version on GitHub Marketplace.
acceptance_criteria: 1. No 'Node.js 20 is deprecated' annotations in CI run output. 2. All actions use their latest stable major version. 3. CI still passes after upgrades.

title: Address dependabot security vulnerability on default branch
description: GitHub reports 1 low-severity vulnerability on the default branch. Run: gh api repos/Michael-A-Kuykendall/muxide/dependabot/alerts to identify the affected package. Apply the fix (usually a version bump in Cargo.toml or a cargo update). Verify the alert clears.
acceptance_criteria: 1. gh api .../dependabot/alerts returns empty or all resolved. 2. The specific vulnerable dependency is identified and fixed. 3. cargo test still passes after the fix. 4. No new regressions introduced.
notes: Files: Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock. Use gh CLI to inspect the alert first before guessing.
close_reason: rand 0.8.5->0.8.6 (RUSTSEC-2026-0097) bumped on main; cargo test green. Alert clears once main is pushed/merged to origin (user: no push yet).

title: Fix release.yml to build cross-platform binaries correctly
description: release.yml has multiple issues: (1) Only builds a Linux binary, not macOS or Windows. (2) The zip command zips the full path instead of just the binary. (3) No cargo test before publishing. Fix: add a matrix strategy for ubuntu/macos/windows, fix the archive commands (tar for unix, zip for windows), add a test step before release, and fix the zip to cd into target/release first.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Release workflow has a matrix with 3 OS targets. 2. Each OS produces a correctly named archive containing only the binary. 3. cargo test runs before cargo build --release. 4. Archives are: muxide-{version}-x86_64-linux.tar.gz, muxide-{version}-x86_64-macos.tar.gz, muxide-{version}-x86_64-windows.zip.

title: Support audio-only fragmented MP4 streams (GitHub issue #2)
description: GitHub issue #2: Support muxing audio tracks without a video track. Currently MuxerBuilder.build() returns MissingVideoConfig if no video is configured. FragmentedMuxer also requires video config. This feature makes video optional in both paths, allowing audio-only MP4 and audio-only fMP4 init+media segments.
design: This is a 13-point feature. Broken into 3 subtasks: muxide-9ue.4.1 (make video optional in Muxer), muxide-9ue.4.2 (audio track box for fMP4), muxide-9ue.4.3 (integration test). Each subtask is independently testable.
acceptance_criteria: 1. MuxerBuilder::build() succeeds with only audio configured (no video). 2. FragmentedMuxer produces valid init segment with audio-only config. 3. Audio-only MP4 plays in VLC and ffprobe validates it. 4. Existing video+audio tests still pass (no regression). 5. New test: audio-only MP4 with AAC-LC, 48kHz, stereo, 100 frames.
notes: Files: src/api.rs (MuxerBuilder::build), src/fragmented.rs (FragmentedMuxer), src/muxer/mp4.rs (finalize path), tests/ (new test file).

title: Make video track optional in MuxerBuilder::build()
description: Currently MuxerBuilder::build() returns MuxerError::MissingVideoConfig when no video is configured. Change this so that video is optional: if no video is configured but audio is, build a Muxer with only an audio track. The Muxer struct's video_track field becomes Option<VideoTrackConfig>. write_video() returns an error if no video track is configured. finish_in_place_with_stats() must handle the no-video case in finalize().
acceptance_criteria: 1. MuxerBuilder::new(Vec::new()).audio(AudioCodec::Aac(AacProfile::Lc), 48000, 2).build() returns Ok. 2. MuxerBuilder::new(Vec::new()).build() (no video, no audio) still returns MissingVideoConfig. 3. write_video() on audio-only muxer returns a new error variant (e.g., VideoNotConfigured). 4. All existing tests still pass.
notes: Files: src/api.rs (Muxer struct, build(), write_video, finish_in_place_with_stats), src/muxer/mp4.rs (finalize).

title: Build audio-only track box for fragmented MP4 init segment
description: FragmentedMuxer currently only supports video tracks. Add audio track support: FragmentConfig needs audio fields (codec, sample_rate, channels). build_moov_fmp4() must emit an audio trak box when audio is configured. build_stsd_fmp4() must emit mp4a or Opus sample entries. The trex in mvex must reference the correct track ID.
acceptance_criteria: 1. FragmentedMuxer with audio-only config produces a valid init segment. 2. Init segment contains ftyp + moov with audio trak + mvex. 3. ffprobe -v error -show_streams init.mp4 shows an audio stream. 4. Existing video fMP4 tests still pass.

title: Integration test: audio-only MP4 and fMP4 end-to-end
description: Write integration tests that exercise the full audio-only path: (1) Non-fragmented: build audio-only Muxer, write 100 AAC frames, finish, verify output is valid MP4 with ffprobe. (2) Fragmented: build audio-only FragmentedMuxer, get init segment, write samples, flush, verify segments. (3) Regression: verify video+audio still works identically.
acceptance_criteria: 1. tests/audio_only.rs exists with at least 3 test functions. 2. All tests pass. 3. At least one test writes output to a tempfile and validates with MP4 box parsing (check for ftyp, moov, mdat). 4. No ffprobe dependency in tests (parse boxes in Rust).
notes: Files: tests/audio_only.rs (new). Depends on: muxide-9ue.4.1 and muxide-9ue.4.2.

title: Dependency upgrades and code cleanup from v0.2.6 audit
description: Follow-up work from the v0.2.6 production audit. Several dependencies are outdated and minor code quality issues remain.
acceptance_criteria: All deps current, no dead public APIs, no Unicode in validation messages

title: Upgrade thiserror from v1 to v2
description: thiserror v2 is the current major. v1 works but is no longer actively developed. Update Cargo.toml to thiserror = "2.0". The v2 derive macro has minor breaking changes: #[error(transparent)] behavior changed, and some attribute syntax differs. Audit every #[derive(Error)] in the codebase: MuxerError (api.rs), Mp4WriterError (mp4.rs), AdtsValidationError (mp4.rs), FragmentedError (fragmented.rs), Vp9Error (vp9.rs). Run cargo test after upgrade.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Cargo.toml has thiserror = "2.0". 2. cargo check exits 0. 3. cargo test exits 0 (all 123+ tests). 4. No thiserror v1 in Cargo.lock. 5. Every error type still formats correctly (spot-check Display output).
notes: Files: Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, possibly api.rs, mp4.rs, fragmented.rs, vp9.rs if derive syntax changed.

title: Replace lazy_static dev-dep with std::sync::LazyLock
description: lazy_static is effectively deprecated. MSRV is 1.81 which stabilized std::sync::LazyLock. Remove lazy_static = "1.4" from [dev-dependencies] in Cargo.toml. Grep for lazy_static usage in tests/ and replace with LazyLock. Run cargo test.
acceptance_criteria: 1. lazy_static is not in Cargo.toml or Cargo.lock. 2. cargo test exits 0. 3. No lazy_static! macro invocations remain anywhere in the codebase.
notes: Files: Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, tests/ files using lazy_static.

title: Upgrade criterion from 0.5 to 0.8
description: criterion 0.5 is unmaintained. Upgrade to 0.8 in [dev-dependencies]. The 0.8 API changed: Criterion::default() is now Criterion::default().with_plots() or similar, and the benchmark macro syntax may differ. Update benches/muxing.rs to match the new API. Run cargo bench to verify benchmarks still execute.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Cargo.toml has criterion = "0.5" removed, criterion = "0.8" added. 2. cargo bench --no-run exits 0 (compile check). 3. cargo bench runs at least one benchmark successfully. 4. No criterion 0.5 in Cargo.lock.

title: Unpin proptest from =1.5.0 to "1"
description: proptest is pinned to exactly 1.5.0 in [dev-dependencies]. Current is 1.11. Change to proptest = "1" to allow semver-compatible updates. Run cargo test --test property_tests to verify all property tests still pass with the newer version.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Cargo.toml has proptest = "1" (not "=1.5.0"). 2. cargo test --test property_tests exits 0. 3. Cargo.lock shows proptest version > 1.5.0.

title: Remove dead public API: is_valid_vp9_frame() in vp9.rs
description: is_valid_vp9_frame() at vp9.rs:255 is pub but never called from production code or tests. It's a 3-line function that duplicates what is_vp9_keyframe already does (checks frame_marker). Either delete it entirely or gate it with #[cfg(test)] if any test references it. Grep the entire codebase first to confirm no callers.
acceptance_criteria: 1. grep -r is_valid_vp9_frame finds zero references in src/ and tests/. 2. cargo check exits 0. 3. cargo test exits 0. 4. The function is either deleted or #[cfg(test)].

title: Replace Unicode checkmarks in validation.rs with ASCII
description: validation.rs uses Unicode symbols (✓, ⚠) in human-readable messages. These may not render in all terminals (Windows cmd, CI logs). Replace ✓ with [OK], ⚠ with [WARN]. Also check if any test assertions match on the Unicode characters and update those too.
acceptance_criteria: 1. grep -P '[\x{2713}\x{26A0}]' src/validation.rs returns zero matches. 2. cargo test exits 0. 3. Messages still convey the same meaning (spot-check output).
notes: Files: src/validation.rs, possibly tests/ if assertions match on symbols.
